title: Marked expansion of exocrine and endocrine pancreas with incretin therapy in humans with increased exocrine pancreas dysplasia and the potential for glucagon-producing neuroendocrine tumors
authors: Butler AE, Campbell-Thompson M, Gurlo T, Dawson DW, Atkinson M, Butler PC
population: Pancreata of age-matched organ donors: 8 with type 2 diabetes treated with incretin therapy, 12 with diabetes on other therapy and 14 without diabetes, from the JDRF nPOD programme
funder: Supported by NIDDK grants DK-059579, DK-061539 and DK-077967, the Larry L. Hillblom Foundation and the Peter and Valerie Kompaniez Foundation; performed with the support of nPOD, sponsored by JDRF.
authorConflicts: No potential conflicts of interest relevant to this article were reported.
result: Incretin-treated diabetic pancreata had about 40% greater mass, increased exocrine proliferation (P < 0.0001) and dysplasia (pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia, P < 0.01), alpha-cell hyperplasia with glucagon-expressing microadenomas in 3 of 8 and one neuroendocrine tumour. Of the 8 incretin-treated donors, treated for 1 year or more, 7 received the DPP-4 inhibitor sitagliptin and 1 the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide; the neuroendocrine tumour occurred in a sitagliptin-treated donor; semaglutide was not studied. FDA and EMA later judged causal claims inconsistent with the totality of data.
